claims: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft is expected to produce a powerful sonic boom on Friday, April 10, 2026, between 5:00 p.m. and 5:15 p.m. PT.
The sonic boom will occur as the Artemis II Orion spacecraft reenters the atmosphere at hypersonic speeds.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft will splash down off the San Diego coast.
Artemis II reentry occurs around 5:00-5:15 p.m. PT.
The sonic boom is likely felt across Southern California.
The sonic boom is caused by the capsule passing through the sound barrier.
The USGS advises that the sonic boom is a normal part of the spacecraft's high-speed return.
The USGS advises that the sonic boom is not an emergency.
The USGS is tracking reports of the sonic boom.
The USGS encourages residents to report if they felt the sonic boom.
The capsule is scheduled to splash down roughly 50-60 miles off the San Diego coast at 5:07 p.m. PT on April 10, 2026.
The splash down marks the end of a 10-day historic mission to the Moon.
